comments.content:
This would let filters have a new "Suck" page, and make siphons not the
only way to clean up air.

Also make filters not one way gd ragzilla

would this be better fulfilled with a "regulated inlet" that tries to keep the room
at a stabilized atmospheric condition? (no more 200% overpressure AI atmos alarms)
and a corresponding regulated vent to go with it (maybe set the 2 of them up at
opposite ends of the room 1 regulating slightly high and 1 low to generate air movement).

Then just grab the output of your inlet to a filter, spit good gases back into the
main loop, and trash into a recovery pipe back to atmos.

or i guess no recovery pipe is needed if you just put it into the main loop, this
would introduce some levels of plasma/CO2 into the main loop though.

That's fine, you can use the vent leading to space set to accept plasma/N2O/whatever
to clear it out of the main loop
Prefer two way filters though, more inlets/vents will be ugly

the problem with 2 way filters is that a combo vent/inlet will not be able to pull
gas out of the room since the pressure in the main line will be higher (and the game
relies on pressure difference between pipes to move gas. thus separate
(pumped/regulated) inlets for each room are required.

Change filter into a sort of exchanger.  Instead of considering how a gas is handled 
in the main pipe, focus on the offshoot pipe.  Change the gas options to Extracting 
(main -> sec), Blocked (no exchange), or Injecting (sec -> main).  The vent/inlet 
should have a pump functionality that is set to the same settings as its connected 
exchanger.

This should allow O2 to be released, with CO2 and other contaminants being captured 
at the same time.
